alex (runtime): Quick design sync: WaveForge generator — goal: capture multi-scale bursts (microbursts inside ramp waves) and long-tail latency shaping. We need kernels + batching heuristic combos to not regress tail.

maya (perf): Love the name :) What's the primary SLO? 99.9 p99 target or 99.99?

alex (runtime): Target p99 <= 120ms for interactive path, p99.9 <= 400ms for background. Also want stable median under high batching.

liam (bench): Plan: replay real traces and synthetic hybrids. Propose a 3-layer waveform: slow ramp (5m), burst trains (30s period) and microbursts (100-500ms spikes). KV cache warmup windows matter.

sara (ml): Important to vary prompt lengths + kv cache hit-rates. Short prompts amplify kernel switch noise.

jonas (infra): We should pin GPU kernels during each experiment to isolate selection cost. Also capture kernel-selection latency histogram from runtime logs.

liam (bench): Agreed. We'll run apples-to-apples: for each workload seed run A: kernel-selection forced, B: runtime default. Seeded RNG. Same VM image + same batcher config.

maya (perf): Can we add an instrumented path to log batching decisions? Minimal overhead: emit one line per batch: BATCH id=.. size=.. latency=.. kernel=.. kv_hits=..

alex (runtime): Yep. Draft of log line:
```
BATCH ts=%s id=%s size=%d kernel=%s kv_hits=%d kv_miss=%d latency_ms=%.2f
```
Will attach a small parser to the harness.

liam (bench): For traffic gen parameters I'm thinking:
- base_qps ramp: 0 -> 1200 qps over 300s
- burst trains: every 30s a 3s high spike at 10x local qps
- microbursts: poisson spikes with mean 60ms inter-arrival inside spikes
- long-tail overlay: add occasional 1-in-200 stalled requests (random delay 3-7s)

sara (ml): Also randomize prompt lengths: 40% short(16-64 tokens), 45% medium(64-512), 15% long(512-2048). KV-access profile: 70% cold, 30% warm in baseline, and separate warm-run experiments.

jonas (infra): Make sure the harness supports sticky routing to avoid cross-node cache pollution when testing KV warm paths.

ci-bot: benchmark:waveforge-run scheduled by @liam (bench) — run id wf-20260318-01

liam (bench): I'll kick off a small pilot today (2 GPU nodes) and share parsed histograms. If we see >10% p99 regression on forced kernel vs default we'll dig into batching heuristics.

maya (perf): Heads-up: kernel-selection path can add 1-3ms if checks are frequent; we might batch decisions at 50ms intervals.

alex (runtime): Good point. Let's instrument both per-request and coalesced modes. Compare cost/benefit.

sara (ml): Can we add a lightweight eval set to run inference outputs to check quality differences when quantized kernels are chosen? We need apples-to-apples quality check.

liam (bench): Yup. Eval run will compute BLEU/ROUGE + a small set of golden prompts. We'll attach output_diffs in artifacts.

alex (runtime): Thanks everyone. Action items:
- liam: implement WaveForge config + parser + run pilot (today)
- maya: add perf flags + batch decision logger
- jonas: ensure sticky routing and kernel pin toggles
- sara: eval set + prompt-length sampler

liam (bench): noted. Will post results thread wf-20260318-01 when done. :rocket:

maya (perf): ping me once the pilot data is posted, I'll run the p99/p99.9 comparisons and kernel breakdown.

alex (runtime): Closing here for now. If anyone sees a quick gotcha reply inline. :raised_hands:
